cards.text: New king in Judah, friend. Ahaz son of Jotham takes the throne at twenty years old and reigns in Jerusalem sixteen years. Up north, Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, is in his seventeenth year.

cards.question: Like David his father, King Ahaz does what is right in the eyes of the LORD his God.
King Ahaz doesn't follow the ways of David his father. Whose ways does he walk in instead?

cards.text: And then it gets darker. Ahaz even sacrifices his son in the fire.

cards.question: When Ahaz sacrifices his son in the fire, whose abominations is he following?

answers.text: The nations driven out before Israel
The nations living down in Egypt
The nations beyond the great river

cards.text: He sacrifices and burns incense on the high places, on the hills and under EVERY green tree, friend, and that is a whole lot of trees. Then Rezin, king of Aram, and Pekah, king of Israel, come up to wage war against Jerusalem.

cards.question: Rezin and Pekah besiege King Ahaz and overcome him.

cards.text: Two kings, a whole siege, and they STILL can't overcome him. But at that time Rezin recovers Elath for Aram and drives out the men of Judah.

cards.question: Rezin drives the men of Judah out of Elath. Who does he send in to live there?

cards.text: So Ahaz sends messengers to Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria. Two kings camped at his walls, and Ahaz scrolls straight to the BIGGEST name in his contacts.

cards.question: In his message to Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, what does Ahaz call himself?

cards.text: Servant AND son? Friend, that's not a letter, that's adoption paperwork, and then comes the ask: "Come up and save me from the hands of the kings of Aram and Israel, who are rising up against me."

cards.question: Ahaz sends a gift to the king of Assyria along with his message. What is it?

answers.text: Silver and gold from the LORD's house and the palace
Horses and chariots from the royal stables
Bronze and iron from the city armories

cards.text: The king of Assyria responds to him and marches up to Damascus. Put some silver and gold in the mix, friend, and suddenly the king of Assyria is ALL ears.

cards.question: The king of Assyria captures Damascus and puts Rezin to death.
The king of Assyria takes the people of Damascus to ___ as captives.

cards.text: With Damascus captured, King Ahaz goes there to meet Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria. And while he's in Damascus, something catches his eye.

cards.question: Something in Damascus catches King Ahaz's eye. What is it?

cards.text: Ahaz sends Uriah the priest a model of the altar and complete plans for building it. That's somebody on vacation texting their contractor a photo and the measurements before they've even unpacked.

cards.question: Uriah the priest finishes building the altar before King Ahaz gets back from Damascus.
When King Ahaz comes back from Damascus and sees the new altar, he approaches it and presents offerings on it.

cards.text: He offers his burnt offering and his grain offering, pours out his drink offering and splatters the blood of his peace offerings on the new altar.
But the bronze altar that stood before the LORD is still right out front, between the new altar and the house of the LORD. Friend, that's a brand new car stuck in the driveway behind the old one.

cards.question: What does King Ahaz do with the bronze altar that stood before the LORD?

answers.text: Moves it to the north side of the new altar
Sends it off to the king of Assyria
Breaks it apart and melts down the bronze

cards.text: Then King Ahaz commands Uriah the priest: the morning burnt offering, the evening grain offering, the king's offerings, all the people's offerings and all the blood go on the great altar. Friend, that new altar just got put on EVERY shift, morning AND evening, no lunch break.

cards.question: Every offering goes on the great altar, but King Ahaz says he'll use the bronze altar to seek ___.
Uriah the priest pushes back on King Ahaz's commands about the altars.

cards.text: Ahaz cuts off the frames of the movable stands, removes the bronze basin from each one and takes down the Sea from the bronze oxen that were under it. One trip to Damascus and this man is renovating like he's got his own home makeover show.

cards.question: King Ahaz takes the Sea down off the bronze oxen and puts it on a ___ base.

cards.text: Then he removes the Sabbath canopy they had built in the temple and closes the royal entryway outside the house of the LORD. Friend, anybody who's been away from Jerusalem is gonna need a MAP just to find the door.

cards.question: Why does King Ahaz remove the Sabbath canopy and close the royal entryway?

answers.text: On account of the king of Assyria
On account of the new altar
On account of Uriah the priest

cards.text: The rest of Ahaz's acts are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah, so if you want the extended cut, that's where it lives. Then Ahaz rests with his fathers and is buried with them in the City of David.

cards.question: After Ahaz is buried in the City of David, which son of his reigns in his place?

findings.problem: Most choice cards are pure discovery that no earlier card sets up, so the baker can only get them right by luck. Examples: whether Ahaz does right like David (stop 1 card 2), whose ways he walks in (stop 1 card 3), whose abominations he follows (stop 1 card 5), whether the siege overcomes him (stop 1 card 7), the Edomites (stop 1 card 9), Kir (stop 1 card 16), the altar (stop 2 card 2), seeking guidance (stop 2 card 10), the stone base (stop 2 card 13) and Hezekiah (stop 2 card 17). Only a handful, like stop 1 card 15 and stop 2 cards 5 and 15, can be reasoned out from what came before.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The card uses the silver and gold gift from 2 Kings 16:8 ("Put some silver and gold in the mix") but cites only 2 Kings 16:9.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card is a bare list of the offerings in 2 Kings 16:13. It has no reaction, comparison or storyteller line, so none of Papa Dorin's voice comes through.

rule.text: A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The car joke ("a brand new car stuck in the driveway behind the old one") presents the LORD's bronze altar as being in the way, which gives a reason for Ahaz moving it. 2 Kings 16:14 gives only its location, not why he moved it. The setup also hints at the answer to card 8, since the fix for a blocking car is to move it.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: "One trip to Damascus and this man is renovating" ties the changes in 2 Kings 16:17 to Ahaz's Damascus trip. The text gives no reason for those changes. The only reason the passage gives is in v18, for different changes, and it is the king of Assyria.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The comparison doesn't match the action. Closing the royal entryway and removing the Sabbath canopy wouldn't make people need a map to find the door, and the line suggests the way into the house of the LORD is gone. A stranger would say "huh?"

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
